To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the introduced search ontology-based XPath specification method enables the reuse of ontologies and XML standards and supports the specification of research question answering by XPath expressions.
we introduced search ontology-based XPath Engineering for querying EHRs by using ontologies and that we evaluated it by using a data collection for Information Retrieval purposes.
search ontology-based XPath Engineering can support research question specification and querying of EHRs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods for the specification of queries on EHRs.
the development of an XML-based query specification method for querying XML-based documents.
the specification and execution of queries in the context of EHRs and the introduction of a new clinical role, the clinical ontologist.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented approach is a promising way to increase precision in EHR research.
the search ontology-based XPath specification is a useful method to specify research questions on XML documents.
the search ontology-based XPath specification of queries is a promising approach to increase the precision of research question answering on EHRs and to reduce the effort for query specification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the usage of search ontology-based XPath engineering is a promising approach to improve precision and recall for querying documents on XML databases.
the usage of search ontologies and search ontology-based XPath expressions is a feasible method to increase the quality of search results in EHRs.
the introduced process is a promising approach that can support research questions answering by using EHRs as data source.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the search ontology is an enabler for the specification of queries on EHRs.
search ontology-based XPath can be used to support the formulation of queries on XML-based EHR data.
the specification and execution of complex XPath expressions can be simplified by search ontology-based engineering.
